title: No Appeal on File

facts.claim: The special empty entry .wh..wh..opq makes its containing directory opaque and hides all children inherited from lower layers.
facts.source_selector: turn751730view0 official OCI Image Specification v1.1.1 opaque whiteout section
facts.draft_exact_string: Under OCI Image Specification v1.1.1, an opaque whiteout hides every lower-layer child of its directory.

facts.claim: Whiteouts affect only resources in lower layers, not files added by the marker-containing layer.
facts.source_selector: turn751730view0 official OCI Image Specification v1.1.1 whiteout lower-layer scope
facts.draft_exact_string: Whiteouts apply only to lower layers, so the same upper layer's status file survives even though its tar entry precedes the opaque marker; the marker itself is hidden after application.

facts.claim: Whiteout entries are applied before other same-layer entries regardless of archive order, and the marker itself is hidden from the resulting filesystem.
facts.source_selector: turn751730view0 official OCI Image Specification v1.1.1 whiteout application-order example
facts.draft_exact_string: Whiteouts apply only to lower layers, so the same upper layer's status file survives even though its tar entry precedes the opaque marker; the marker itself is hidden after application.

facts.claim: OCI image manifests list filesystem layers in base-to-upper stack order.
